accuracyFacts: Class declarations and expressions execute in strict mode; class declarations have lexical binding initialization and a temporal dead zone.
Class constructors cannot be called without new.
A base class instance's fields initialize before its constructor body. A derived class's fields initialize immediately after super() returns and before the remaining derived constructor body.
Public class fields use define-own-property semantics and do not invoke an inherited setter as an assignment would.
Static fields and static initialization blocks run in source order during class definition evaluation; a base class completes static initialization before a derived class.
Private names are lexically scoped and are not ordinary string or Symbol properties; they cannot be dynamically created or accessed outside authorized lexical code.
A Proxy around a private-branded object does not itself possess the target's private elements; brand checks against the proxy return false and private access through it throws TypeError.
Class constructor .prototype is a non-writable own property. Class methods/accessors are non-enumerable shared properties; public fields are own writable, enumerable, configurable data properties.

Public static fields and methods named prototype are early errors. Instance and static class fields named constructor are early errors. A static method named constructor is allowed but is not the class constructor.
A class may extend null, giving its prototype object a null prototype, but must define a constructor that returns an object directly rather than trying to call super().
A private-name brand check using #name in value checks whether the object has that class's private element; it is not equivalent to instanceof.

A derived constructor cannot access this before super() initializes it. A derived constructor may return an object explicitly; primitive returns are only permitted when super() has initialized this, otherwise construction throws.

Methods and accessors are installed on the relevant prototype or constructor; fields are per-instance or per-class own properties and their initializer runs at the specified construction/evaluation time.
Decorators are outside this lesson's scope because they are not part of the ECMAScript 2026 standard edition.
